title: Account Executive
description:

This role focuses on generating new opportunities, managing the full sales cycle, and selling our full line of data center services, including colocation, cloud, and managed services, to organizations not yet engaged with our solutions.

The successful candidate will possess a strong track record of new business sales success and must demonstrate exceptional critical thinking, negotiation, organizational, and time‑management skills.

This role is ideal for someone experienced in technology sales who consistently succeeds using a consultative sales process such as Solution Selling.

Capitalize on one of technology's biggest growth markets. Join Flexential and help organizations navigate the future of hybrid cloud, AI-ready infrastructure, and digital transformation. This is a rare opportunity to build a territory in a high-demand market where complex business challenges translate into strategic, high-value sales opportunities.

Key Responsibilities and Essential Job Functions

  • Meet and/or exceed all quota requirements.
  • Develop and execute sales territory plans.
  • Sell into an assigned set of prospects that currently do not do business with Flexential.
  • Determine and set the appropriate sales strategy to position and close complex sales opportunities in a competitive colocation, cloud and managed services market.
  • Develop and build relationships with prospective customer executives, technical staff and key strategic partners.
  • Develop technical responses and strategy for RFP’s as a member of the account team.
  • Manage multiple priorities and multi-task effectively.
  • Track prospect and sales activities in Salesforce.com.
  • Perform other duties as required and assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience demonstrating a documented path of sales success
  • A successful documented path of sales success selling to prospects
  • Solid track record calling on business decision makers within the IT organization in a highly competitive market
  • Proven ability to build relationships throughout the customer organization
  • Experience selling managed services, IT Infrastructure, software-as-a-service or application hosting is ideal
  • Bachelor's degree or any combination of education & related experience that would demonstrate possession of the knowledge and abilities needed to achieve success in this position
  • Ability to travel to assigned territories
  • High-energy individual with a positive attitude, good teamwork skills and exceptional customer presentation experience
  • Strong questioning and listening skills.
  • Able to translate innate curiosity into account progress
  • Presents a professional and credible face to the customer and prospect
  • Self-directed, self-motivated and results oriented – possesses the drive and determination to succeed.
  • Willing to work hard, knows how to work smart
  • Persistent but pragmatic: willing to be flexible and adaptable to change
  • Critical thinker – can address the challenges presented during sales conversation
  • Possess the ability to continually self-educate to maintain a broad knowledge of complex products, services and selling skills

title: Business Relationship Manager
location_raw: Charlotte, NC; CO - Denver Corp; PA - Collegeville
description:
The Business Relationship Manager (BRM) serves as the strategic interface between business functions and the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), assuring technology investments, capabilities, and services are aligned with organizational objectives and deliver measurable business value.

Acting as a trusted advisor, consultant, and relationship leader, the BRM partners with business stakeholders to understand priorities, challenges, opportunities, and desired outcomes, translating them into scalable, compliant, and sustainable technology solutions.

The BRM helps business partners navigate OCIO processes and services, assuring requests are understood in the context of business priorities, outcomes, urgency, strategic alignment, and value realization.

This role is focused on building trusted relationships, shaping demand, defining business capabilities, improving business processes, and facilitating effective governance and decision-making. The BRM serves as a primary liaison between the business and OCIO, helping clarify needs before work enters delivery channels and ensuring initiatives are aligned to portfolio priorities, enterprise standards, available capacity, and long-term technology strategy.

The role requires strong business acumen, technical fluency, process improvement expertise, executive communication skills, and the ability to bridge strategy, process, technology, and delivery.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Relationship Management & Business Partnership

  • Serve as the primary strategic point of contact between assigned business functions and OCIO.
  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with business leaders, stakeholders, and technology partners.
  • Develop a deep understanding of business objectives, operating models, challenges, regulatory requirements, and strategic priorities.
  • Act as a trusted advisor, helping business partners agnostically understand available technology services, capabilities, governance processes, and investment considerations.
  • Develop and maintain IT Project Roadmaps with business partners.
  • Maintain continuous visibility into stakeholder needs, priorities, risks, and opportunities.
  • Assure business partners understand how requests are evaluated, prioritized, funded, and advanced through portfolio and delivery processes.
  • Facilitate productive collaboration between business stakeholders, architecture, security, data, AI, delivery, operations, and portfolio management teams.
  • Influence decision-making without direct authority and help align competing priorities across stakeholder groups.
  • Partner with SIO and PFLT to assure alignment on strategic priorities and initiatives.

Demand Management, Demand Shaping & Portfolio Alignment

  • Lead demand discovery, intake, shaping, prioritization, and governance activities for assigned business areas.
  • Help clarify business needs, desired outcomes, timing expectations, success measures, urgency, and value drivers before work enters delivery channels with a focus on achieving business outcomes.
  • Translate business requests into well-defined demand, capability requirements, opportunity briefs, and initiative proposals.
  • Develop business cases and KPIs to track value of business outcomes and solutions delivered.
  • Support demand shaping by connecting requests to enterprise strategy, portfolio priorities, regulatory requirements, available capacity, and technology roadmaps.

  • Ensure work is routed through the appropriate intake, governance, funding, and delivery processes.

Business Process Excellence & Capability Planning

  • Lead process optimization, standardization, automation, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Champion change management activities for new business processes partnering with the respective business units to help drive adoption.
  • Develop multi-year business capability roadmaps aligned with strategic objectives and enterprise technology plans.
  • Facilitate process-centered discussions that translate desired business outcomes into integrated technology solutions.

A successful Business Relationship Manager will:

  • Improve the quality and strategic alignment of technology demand.

  • Increase adoption and reuse of enterprise platforms and capabilities.

title: Commercial Operations Associate
description:
The Commercial Operations Associate is responsible for supporting the end to end Non Recurring Charge (NRC) quoting process, managing purchase order creation, and conducting detailed vendor quote analysis. This role ensures accurate cost recovery through true up processes and standardized markup. The Associate works cross functionally with Sales, Finance, Procurement, Product and Operations to drive operational efficiency, financial accuracy.
Key Responsibilities and Essential Job Functions
  • Manage full lifecycle NRC quoting, including requirements validation, scoping, pricing, and timely delivery to Sales.
  • Ensure quotes comply with internal standards, margin requirements, and contractual obligations.
  • Partner with Operations teams to validate technical accuracy and feasibility.
  • Create and submit purchase orders for equipment, project materials, and vendor services aligned to approved quotes and budgets.
  • Track PO status, receipt, and delivery milestones to ensure timely project execution.
  • Coordinate with Finance and Procurement to resolve discrepancies or exceptions.
  • Review and analyze vendor proposals for accuracy, completeness, and alignment with project scope.
  • Compare vendor pricing, terms, and lead times to ensure cost‑effective sourcing decisions.
  • Identify variances or cost risks and escalate recommendations for approval.
  • Conduct true‑up analysis to reconcile estimated vs. actual project costs.
  • Apply standardized markup structures to ensure full cost recovery and margin protection.
  • Document and communicate final cost settlements to internal stakeholders and update financial systems as required.
  • Work closely with Sales, Finance, Operations teams to improve quoting accuracy and streamline commercial workflows.
  • Support process improvements and documentation within the Commercial Operations function.
  • Maintain accurate records of quotes, vendor data, POs, and true‑up documents.
  • Prepare reporting on quote cycle times, cost variances, and PO trends to support leadership insights and continuous improvement.
Required Qualifications
  • Analytical Thinking – Able to break down cost components and identify discrepancies.
  • Commercial Acumen – Understands pricing, margins, and cost recovery principles.
  • Collaboration – Works effectively across diverse teams and functional areas.
  • Process Orientation – Ensures accuracy, consistency, and adherence to workflow standards.
  • Communication – Provides clear and professional written and verbal updates.

title: Data Center Operations Technician III
description:

A strong understanding of facilities infrastructure, Windows operating systems, PC troubleshooting and management applications is expected in this role. A Data Center Technician III must be able to demonstrate the ability to represent Flexential, both professionally and technically, during interactions with customers and internal resources in a calm and professional manner.

  • Lead and mentor DCT I and II team members by training on Technical Operations best practices, auditing procedures, ticket analysis, communication standards, and provisioning workflows.
  • Serve as a trusted peer resource, providing guidance across operational tasks, documentation, and escalation paths.
  • Own project-level responsibilities, including resource allocation, task delegation, and deadline setting for provisioning and maintenance efforts.

  • Validate and translate complex instructions for Remote Hands tasks, ensuring alignment with customer environments and resolving discrepancies.
  • Perform maintenance and PRJTASK requests independently, with full ownership of execution and quality.
  • Model professionalism and operational excellence, consistently reinforcing standards and supporting team development.
  • Demonstrate reliability and flexibility in supporting 24x7x365 operations, including working varied shifts as needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned, contributing to a high-performing, collaborative, and resilient data center environment.

  • Experience in a 24/7 production environment
  • Strong critical thinking skills

title: Director, HR Business Partners
description:
The Director, HR Business Partners leads the team of HR business partners who provide strategic support to leaders across every function at Flexential. The Director sets the standard for how business partnership is practiced here: close enough to the business to understand what drives results, candid enough to challenge a leader's thinking, and disciplined enough to keep decisions consistent, fair, and defensible. The role carries direct partnership responsibility for a portfolio of senior leaders while coaching a small team to do the same across the rest of the organization.

The HR business partner team is the front door to People & Culture. Leaders and team members should be able to bring any people question to a business partner and get either an answer or a fast, warm handoff to the right expertise in HRIS, data and analytics, learning and development, compensation and benefits, or talent acquisition. The Director owns that experience end to end, making sure the door is easy to find, quick to open, and never a dead end.

As a member of the People & Culture leadership team, the Director works in close collaboration with every P&C function to ensure the programs and initiatives the team drives are the ones that help the Flexential team reach its business and growth goals.

The Director reports to the Chief People Officer and leads a small team of HR business partners supporting leaders across all functions and locations. The role sits on the People & Culture leadership team and partners peer to peer with the leaders of total rewards and HR operations, talent acquisition, learning and development, and people analytics. Client groups may include corporate functions, sales, operations, and engineering, with assignments adjusted as the business grows.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Business Partnership

  • Partner with senior leaders on the people implications of their business plans: how the team is structured, where capability gaps sit, what the next twelve months of hiring and development need to look like, and which decisions carry organizational risk.
  • Bring workforce data and outside perspective into planning conversations early, rather than reacting after a decision is made.
  • Translate business strategy into a practical people agenda for each client group and hold both sides accountable to it.

Team Leadership

  • Hire, coach, and develop the HR business partner team, setting clear expectations for consultative skill, judgment, and responsiveness.
  • Balance portfolio assignments so coverage is equitable and no leader is left without support.
  • Create the routines that make a small team feel bigger: shared case review, consistent documentation, calibrated approaches to recurring situations, and deliberate development plans for each partner.
  • Model the standard of service the team is expected to deliver.

Performance Management

  • Own how performance management is practiced in the field.
  • Coach managers through goal setting, ongoing feedback, review cycles, calibration, and the harder conversations that follow, including performance improvement plans and separations.
  • Work with learning and development to build manager capability rather than absorbing the work on managers' behalf, so that the quality of performance conversations rises across the organization over time.

Employee Relations

  • Oversee employee relations across the organization, ensuring investigations are timely, thorough, well documented, and consistent in outcome.
  • Advise leaders on risk, precedent, and legal exposure, escalating to the Chief People Officer and to counsel when the situation warrants.
  • Track themes across cases and convert them into systemic fixes such as policy changes, manager training, or structural adjustments, so recurring issues are addressed at the source.

Career and Talent Planning

  • Lead talent reviews, succession planning, and career pathing for supported client groups.
  • Make sure every leadership team has a current view of its bench strength, its critical roles, its flight risks, and its high-potential team members, along with a plan for each.
  • Partner with learning and development on development experiences and with talent acquisition on where to build versus buy, and ensure internal candidates are genuinely considered for open roles.

Retention and Engagement

  • Use engagement survey results, turnover data, exit and stay interviews, and direct listening to identify where the team member experience is falling short, then work with leaders on specific, time-bound actions.
  • Partner with total rewards on pay equity and retention risk, and with the broader P&C team on the moments that shape retention most, including onboarding, promotion, manager transitions, and the first year in role.

Front Door to P&C

  • Ensure leaders and team members can access People & Culture expertise efficiently. The business partner is the single point of entry: resolving what can be resolved directly, routing quickly to HRIS, data and analytics, learning and development, compensation and benefits, or talent acquisition when specialist depth is needed, and staying accountable for the outcome through to resolution.
  • Establish and monitor service standards for responsiveness and follow-through, and make the path to help obvious to every leader.

P&C Team Leadership and Collaboration

  • Contribute to the strategy, priorities, and annual plan of the People & Culture function as a member of its leadership team.
  • Bring the voice of the business into P&C decision making, testing proposed programs against what leaders and team members actually need and what the organization can absorb.
  • Collaborate with every P&C function on design and rollout, and serve as an advocate for the function's work in the field so initiatives land as intended and drive the business and growth goals they were built to support.

Core Competencies

The following competencies describe how the role is expected to be performed and form the basis for how performance in the role will be assessed:

  • Business Acumen: Understands how Flexential makes money, what pressures each client group faces, and how people decisions affect those outcomes.
  • Strategic Influence: Earns a seat in planning conversations and shapes decisions before they are made, without relying on positional authority.
  • Coaching and Candor: Tells leaders what they need to hear, builds their capability rather than doing the work for them, and stays in the relationship afterward.
  • Judgment and Risk Management: Weighs fairness, precedent, and legal exposure quickly, and knows when to decide and when to escalate.
  • Team Leadership: Develops business partners into trusted advisors and creates the consistency that lets a small team cover a large organization.
  • Data Fluency: Works comfortably with workforce data and turns it into a clear recommendation rather than a report.
  • Collaboration Across P&C: Partners with every P&C function so programs are designed with the field in mind and land well when they reach leaders.

Measures of Success

Within the first year, success in this role is visible in the following ways:

  • Leaders describe their business partner as one of the first calls they make when facing a people decision, not a step they take after the fact.
  • Performance review and calibration cycles are completed on time, with noticeably higher quality of documentation and feedback.
  • Employee relations matters are resolved within agreed timeframes, with consistent outcomes and clean documentation.
  • Every leadership team supported has a current talent review and succession plan for its critical roles.
  • Regrettable attrition and engagement measures move in the intended direction in the client groups supported.
  • Requests routed into People & Culture reach the right expertise quickly and close out without the requester having to chase them.

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in human resources, business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of progressive human resources experience, including at least 3 years partnering directly with senior leaders.
  • 2+ years leading, coaching, and developing HR professionals.
  • Demonstrated depth in performance management, employee relations, organizational design, and talent and succession planning.
  • Working knowledge of employment law and multi-jurisdiction compliance obligations across the locations supported.
  • Proven ability to turn workforce data into recommendations that leaders understand and act on.
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving, growth-oriented environment with competing priorities and incomplete information.

Preferred

  • SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or an equivalent senior HR certification.
  • Experience in data center, technology infrastructure, or another capital-intensive environment with a distributed, always-on workforce.
  • Experience supporting an organization through rapid growth, acquisition integration, or significant transformation.
  • Fluency with a modern HRIS platform and people analytics tooling.

title: VP, Data Center Operations
description:
Flexential is seeking a proven, enterprise scale operations leader to serve as Vice President, Data Center Operations.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this executive will lead the performance, discipline, and daily execution of a national portfolio of 40+ mission critical multi-tenant and wholesale data centers and a team of 300+ people. The role carries broad accountability for regional operations, critical environment performance, physical security, environmental health and safety, and the leadership of teams responsible for operating highly reliable data center infrastructure in support of customer workloads.

This leader will own the operational heartbeat of the portfolio.

The Vice President will be responsible for ensuring that every facility is run with rigor, consistency, technical depth, and a relentless commitment to uptime, safety, and customer confidence. The scope is highly centered on mission critical execution and requires deep command of MEP systems, critical power and cooling infrastructure, maintenance discipline, operational readiness, and incident leadership.

The role is designed for a leader who is energized by scale, complexity, and the opportunity to build. This executive will inherit a meaningful operating footprint and will be expected to elevate performance, strengthen leadership capability, drive consistency across regions, and create an environment in which high standards are translated into repeatable, measurable results.

For the right candidate, this is an opportunity to make a visible enterprise impact and help define the future operating model of a rapidly evolving digital infrastructure platform.

Why This Role Matters

Flexential’s data center portfolio sits at the center of critical customer operations. As the business continues to scale, the company requires a senior operations executive who can bring strong field credibility, strategic thinking, disciplined execution, and the ability to lead through complexity.

The Vice President, Data Center Operations will play a central role in ensuring that facilities perform safely and consistently, that teams are equipped and aligned, and that the operating model can support continued growth with confidence.

This is not a staff or advisory role. It is an operating role in the truest sense. The leader in this position will be accountable for what happens in the field, how teams perform, how incidents are led, how risk is managed, and how the company turns institutional standards, insights, and operational expectations into world class execution.

Role Scope and Organizational Context

The Vice President, Data Center Operations owns the “run” component of the company’s operating model. The role is accountable for executing within the framework established by enterprise partners responsible for standards, training, operational enablement, controls, and intelligence.

This position is therefore best suited for a leader who understands how to partner closely across functions, consume and operationalize enterprise guidance effectively, and hold field teams accountable for disciplined adoption and execution.

The role is distinct from groups that create standards, training content, controls platforms, or operational intelligence. Instead, the Vice President ensures that these inputs are translated into performance at the site and regional level.

This clear separation of responsibilities is intentional and creates the conditions for sharper accountability, stronger execution, and better enterprise alignment.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Center Operations Leadership

  • Lead all day-to-day operations across the company’s data center portfolio, with accountability for execution, reliability, workforce performance, and site level discipline.
  • Provide leadership to regional operations leaders and site teams, establishing clear expectations, strong operating rhythms, and visible accountability for performance.
  • Drive consistency across facilities while preserving appropriate agility to respond to local operational realities, customer needs, and evolving business priorities.
  • Build a performance culture rooted in safety, ownership, responsiveness, preparation, and continuous improvement.
  • Drive rigorous maintenance, data quality, and operational adoption of DCIM, BMS, building automation, and controls platforms to strengthen visibility, standardize execution, and improve portfolio performance.

Critical Facility, Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing Leadership

  • Own the operational performance and lifecycle review of mission critical facility infrastructure, including electrical, mechanical, plumbing, cooling, life safety, critical power, generation, UPS, switchgear, and supporting systems required to sustain uptime and customer confidence.
  • Ensure strong maintenance discipline, technical readiness, facility inspections, incident preparedness, and operational rigor across all sites.
  • Lead with credibility in highly technical, MEP intensive environments where precision, sound judgment, and operational discipline are essential.

Safety, Security, and Risk Management

  • Provide executive oversight for Environmental Health and Safety programs across the operations organization.
  • Lead physical security operations and reinforce disciplined execution of site access, life safety, and risk management protocols.
  • Promote a culture in which safety and risk awareness are foundational to every operating decision and every level of the organization.

Operational Execution of Enterprise Standards

  • Translate enterprise standards, training, reporting, operational intelligence, and controls related insights into high-quality execution across the field organization.
  • Ensure teams understand expectations, adopt the required operating practices, and meet the company’s standards for consistency and performance.
  • Create strong follow through mechanisms, so operational policies and expectations are not only communicated, but fully implemented and sustained.

Cross Functional Leadership

  • Partner closely with teams responsible for construction, commissioning, operational enablement, controls, analytics, and process improvement to ensure clean handoffs, strong readiness, and effective execution across the portfolio.
  • Provide field informed feedback that strengthens how future capacity is delivered, how standards are matured, and how enterprise systems better support operations at scale.
  • Act as a trusted enterprise leader who can balance collaboration with clarity of ownership and execution accountability.

Talent and Organizational Development

  • Build, coach, and develop a high performing operations leadership team capable of leading at scale.
  • Strengthen bench depth, succession planning, and leadership capability across regions and sites.
  • Attract and retain strong talent by creating a demanding, mission driven, and highly respected operations culture.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is an experienced mission critical operations executive who combines technical credibility with strong people leadership and enterprise level judgment.

This individual will bring a deep understanding of facility operations and MEP systems, along with a demonstrated ability to lead across geographies, improve consistency, strengthen culture, and raise the performance of complex operating teams.

The successful candidate will be equally comfortable in executive discussions and field environments. They will know how to lead during incidents, how to build trust with experienced operators, how to make difficult decisions with confidence, and how to create alignment across functions without losing sight of accountability.

They will be energized by the opportunity to shape an organization, elevate standards of performance, and leave a durable mark on the operating model.

Required Qualifications

  • Ten or more years of progressive leadership experience in mission critical operations, industrial operations, or similarly complex environments where uptime, safety, and technical discipline are paramount.
  • Significant experience leading multi site operations teams with accountability for performance across multiple geographies.
  • Deep expertise in data center or similarly critical mechanical, electrical, and plumbing intensive environments.
  • Demonstrated success improving operational consistency, workforce performance, reliability, and execution quality at scale.
  • Experience leading through incidents, elevated operational risk, and periods of organizational growth or transformation.
  • Strong command of safety, compliance, physical security, and risk management principles in operational settings.
  • Excellent executive communication skills, strong judgment, and the ability to influence across functions and levels.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience within colocation, enterprise, wholesale, multi-tenant data center, or other mission critical infrastructure environments.
  • Experience partnering with controls, building automation, DCIM, or operational intelligence teams in support of portfolio performance.
  • Experience supporting new market expansion, major facility commissioning, or large-scale infrastructure growth.
  • A track record of building strong regional leadership teams and advancing operational leadership capability over time.

Measures of Success

Success in this role will be measured by sustained improvement in safety performance, uptime and reliability, maintenance quality, operational readiness, incident effectiveness, site level consistency, and the strength and engagement of the operations leadership team.

The Vice President will also be evaluated on their ability to build strong partnerships across the enterprise, translate standards into execution, and create a high confidence operating environment that can scale with the business.

Opportunity Statement

This role offers the opportunity to lead one of the most important functions in the company. It is a chance to operate at meaningful scale, influence enterprise performance, shape a critical leadership team, and build the systems, rigor, and culture required to support long term growth.

For a candidate who thrives in mission critical environments and wants the chance to lead from the front, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact.

Compensation

Base Pay Range: Annualized salary range offered for this position is estimated to be $225,000 - $290,000. However, the actual pay range depends on each candidate’s experience, location, and qualifications.

Variable Pay: Discretionary annual bonus, based on personal and company performance.
